entities.name: Kemal Idris
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ahmed Kemal Idris (died 2010-07-28) was a pivotal Indonesian Army general whose career spanned the Indonesian National Revolution and the tumultuous early decades of independent Indonesia, significantly influencing the nation's political trajectory and military ascendancy. Emerging as a fierce guerrilla leader against Dutch colonial forces, Idris later became a key figure in the post-independence military establishment, known for his staunch anti-communism and his instrumental role in the events surrounding the 1965 coup attempt and the subsequent rise of the New Order regime.

Idris first rose to prominence during the Indonesian National Revolution (1945-1949), notably leading resistance efforts after the Dutch reoccupied Yogyakarta in 1948. He played a significant part in the March 1st General Offensive (Serangan Umum 1 Maret 1949), a coordinated military assault that temporarily recaptured Yogyakarta and bolstered Indonesia's diplomatic position. Following independence, he steadily climbed the military ranks, eventually commanding the Army Strategic Reserve Command (Kostrad) for West Java. His strategic position and loyalty to General Suharto proved crucial during the 1965 crisis, when he helped consolidate military power and orchestrate the violent suppression of the Indonesian Communist Party (PKI).

His actions contributed directly to the entrenchment of the Indonesian military's political power and the establishment of Suharto's authoritarian New Order, which dominated Indonesia for over three decades. Idris's career exemplifies the generation of Indonesian military leaders who transitioned from nationalist freedom fighters to powerful political actors, shaping the nation's internal security doctrines and its anti-communist foreign policy during the Cold War. His legacy remains intertwined with the debates surrounding military intervention in civilian politics and the human rights abuses committed during the 1965 purges.
